officialTitle: Neoadjuvant Nivolumab plus Chemotherapy in Resectable Lung Cancer

design.blinding: Open-label; EFS and pCR by blinded independent review
design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: A total of 358 patients were concurrently assigned to receive nivolumab plus chemotherapy (179 patients) or chemotherapy alone (179 patients).
design.notes: Three cycles of neoadjuvant therapy followed by surgery.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding nivolumab to neoadjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy improve EFS and pCR in resectable stage IB–IIIA NSCLC?

pico.intervention: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus platinum-based chemotherapy for three cycles, then surgery
pico.comparator: Neoadjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy alone, then surgery
pico.outcomes: Primary: EFS and pCR. Key secondary: OS

publications.title: Neoadjuvant Nivolumab plus Chemotherapy in Resectable Lung Cancer.
publications.label: Primary EFS/pCR analysis

publications.title: Overall Survival with Neoadjuvant Nivolumab plus Chemotherapy in Lung Cancer.
publications.label: Final overall survival analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: The median event-free survival was 31.6 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 30.2 to not reached) with nivolumab plus chemotherapy and 20.8 months (95% CI, 14.0 to 26.7) with chemotherapy alone (hazard ratio for disease progression, disease recurrence, or death, 0.63; 97.38% CI, 0.43 to 0.91; P = 0.005).
The percentage of patients with a pathological complete response was 24.0% (95% CI, 18.0 to 31.0) and 2.2% (95% CI, 0.6 to 5.6), respectively (odds ratio, 13.94; 99% CI, 3.49 to 55.75; P<0.001).
At the first prespecified interim analysis, the hazard ratio for death was 0.57 (99.67% CI, 0.30 to 1.07) and did not meet the criterion for significance.

The final analysis of overall survival significantly favored neoadjuvant nivolumab plus chemotherapy over chemotherapy (hazard ratio for death, 0.72; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.523 to 0.998; P = 0.048). At a median follow-up of 68.4 months, the 5-year overall survival was 65.4% with nivolumab plus chemotherapy and 55.0% with chemotherapy alone

outcomes.endpointLabel: 5-year OS by pCR status (nivolumab-plus-chemotherapy arm only)
outcomes.analysisLabel: Final OS analysis (exploratory, by pathological response)
outcomes.population: Nivolumab plus chemotherapy arm, pCR vs no pCR
outcomes.sourceQuote: the 5-year overall survival in the nivolumab-plus-chemotherapy group was 95.3% (95% CI, 82.7 to 98.8) among the patients with a pathological complete response and 55.7% (95% CI, 46.9 to 63.7) among those without such a response

safety.sourceQuote: Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 33.5% of the patients in the nivolumab-plus-chemotherapy group and in 36.9% of those in the chemotherapy-alone group.

safety.description: Proportion of randomised patients who underwent surgery
safety.sourceQuote: Of the patients who underwent randomization, 83.2% of those in the nivolumab-plus-chemotherapy group and 75.4% of those in the chemotherapy-alone group underwent surgery.

strengths: Randomised phase III with EFS and pCR assessed by blinded independent review
Short (three-cycle) neoadjuvant course without adjuvant immunotherapy
limitations: No adjuvant immunotherapy component, so contribution of each phase cannot be compared with perioperative regimens
Exploratory pCR-stratified survival analyses are non-randomised comparisons

clinicalImplications.text: Established neoadjuvant nivolumab plus platinum chemotherapy before resection as a standard for resectable NSCLC without contraindication to immunotherapy, with an overall survival benefit at final analysis.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Three cycles of chemo-immunotherapy before surgery did not compromise operability; pCR is strongly associated with long-term survival but is not a substitute endpoint for decisions in the individual patient.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstracts of PMIDs 35403841 (primary) and 40454642 (final OS).
